summary: Buckingham County, VA fire tower built before 1941 and reported rotten by 1954; the summit was cleared in 1963 for an AT&T troposcatter relay whose concrete reflectors remain on private land.

facts.status_note: Register says the tower was reported rotten on the ground in 1954 and the site was cleared in 1963 for an AT&T troposcatter facility; the relay's concrete reflectors remain

access.note: Private land; the CLUI entry says the site is privately owned and used as part of a residence, and the 2013 WSET report asks readers not to try to see it

events.note: Reported rotten on the ground in 1954; the register's Removed field reads 'by 1954'
Site cleared for an AT&T troposcatter communications facility
Property bought from the government by a landowner, who built a house on the site

corrections.why: The register's Built field reads 'before 1941'; no source gives 1941

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register spells it Spear Mountain; the Cold War inventory and the WSET report say Spears Mountain. The register's coordinates match the Forest Fire Lookout Association's, so these describe one place.
Register says the summit was cleared in 1963; the Cold War inventory says the relay began operating around 1964-1965. Clearing came first, so the dates agree.

notes_for_editor: The 1963 clearing and the 1964-1965 start of operation are a sequence, not a conflict. The brief's built date (1941) is not in the source; the register says before 1941. The 2005 sale is taken from the WSET report and is not named in the story to protect the private landowner. No source describes the lookout tower's design, staffing, or fires. The register's 1954 description is the only account of the tower itself.
